The things a PoE loot filter can do are very limited. A good rule of thumb is: If you can't do it on FilterBlade, it's likely not possible in PoE. You can:Add colors (text, border, background) with opacity, but no gradients, and no changing the border widthAdd beams and minimap iconsPlay one from the 26 sounds with a given volume + NEW: play those sounds in a way that tells where in the game world that item dropped. + NEW: Play custom sound files on your PC.Set a size from 18 to 45. Nothing bigger or smaller than that.Things we can NOT do include but are not limited to:Filter by unique name. Only filtering by BaseType is possible. And many BaseTypes have multiple uniques. A filter cannot tell which one of those it is, even if it's identified.Change the font itselfEdit the font of chests, breach hands, masters, etc to be bigger or better visible.Detect the 'Tier' of an item (PoE2 only).Detect the mods of unidentified items, or the specific (corruption-) implicits of any item, not which mod is fractured.Only show items that are allocated to me when playing in groups.Only show items for a given time and hide them after x seconds.

The sync-to-poe feature saves the filter directly in your POE-account. You can find your filter in the ingame settings (click 'refresh' first). You need to login for the first (this is a safe login, search for OAUTH here for details, we don't get any of your credentials). Download gives you the filter file directly. You will then need to place the file into the "%userprofile%/Documents/My Games/Path of Exile" (or Path of Exile 2) repository for it to work. Both have their up and downsides. Sync is generally speaking more comfortable, but it 'caches' the filter if multiple syncs are done in quick succession and it might take up to 10 min to arrive ingame. New syncs seem to always arrive instantly. It also doesn't work when the POE servers are down/updating. Download on the other hand takes a few extra clicks and spams your download folder, but is very reliable.

To give you a POE analogy. If filters would be a POE skilltree, modules would be jewels. A filter can include 0 to 15 modules and a single module can affect multiple filters. Modules are great if you want to have the same set of changes across multiple filters. For instance if you want to reuse the same style or tiering you can save these in a module and then apply them onto one or multiple filters. Every time you load a save, it fetches the latest version of the module. You can also browse for public and 'official' modules on the overview screen!

The Ruthless gamemode requires a completely different type of filter - both technically as well as regarding the logic of filtering. You can't use a normal filter in Ruthless or the other way around. Ruthless filters also don't allow you to fully hide items or make them transparent. You can select the Ruthless filter on the Overview page. It currently has NO styles or strictnesses. When exporting a Ruthless filter, we will automatically fix Hide-rules and also the file extension in order for it to work ingame.

Depends on which you are using:Normal / Positional sounds are built in to the game, you don't need to download anything. This includes the Shaper voice lines.Our Community sounds from PoE streamers are hosted on FilterBlade. You are offered to download them when downloading or syncing the filter.If you use a module, its creator should have provided a download link for the sound files in the module description, as we are unable to host these files ourselves due to copyright reasons.

Another tricky part are strictnesses. The strictness you used when creating a module doesn't directly matter, but it allows you to do changes that aren't possible otherwise. For example you can't have a module that disables Chancing Bases when you work on a low stirctness, because that section is already disabled, meaning it wouldn't be a change and therefore not saved. Changing to a high strictness allows you to do and save this change.

The SC and HC Economy filters adjust their tiering every 4 hours. Every section that is economy based is marked with 'chaos orbs'. This is done in order to keep the filter up-to-date with the live economy and meta state. If suddenly something becomes more expensive/cheaper (due to a build becoming popular, game changes or a new tech being discovered), you will know. However, you CAN control this behaviour:

We added a lot of useful features into the right-click menu. Just rightclick e.g. a BaseType within a tierlist to have the option to move it into a different (or new) tier. Or right-click the class-selection GUI to see options to (de-)select all options with one click. There are a lot of options. The 'Show Priority' one can be very useful to check which rule has priority when you're not sure.

The Economy (Eco) filter tracks the live economy. Its tiering for currency, uniques, fragments, gems and 20+ other lists refreshes every 4 hours, and that's what most players want. The Stable filter ignores economy updates and only changes a couple of times per league, which makes it a good choice for SSF or if you simply want a fixed, predictable filter that doesn't move around on you.

Another reason for odd behaviors is the fact that your filter might already have changes in the section that the module edits and overwrites it. You can try Shift-Rightclicking a section to hard-reset it, which doesn't set the section back to its initial values, but instead deletes all of your local changes, causing the module to take effect again. This can sometimes make a difference.

First of all ensure that you're using a somewhat up-to-date filter version. We're developers, not fortune-tellers. Then filters can NOT tell uniques of the same basetype apart. For instance 'leather belt' uniques can't be distinguished. Your belt might be a super-expensive headhunter or a worthless wurm's molt. These uniques are usually marked with a blue star on the minimap

Like normal filter-saveStates, modules work not by saving the current, final state of the filter, but by saving the changes you made. Meaning if something is back on its initial value, it doesn't count as change and is therefore not applied in the filter. This can happen a lot in ever-changing parts like tierlists, where items move often and rules get disabled all the time.

Disable: This removes the rule from the filter, this means that rule will not and cannot catch any item and it leaves the other rules in the filter to handle the item. You should only be disabling rules if it is the default option in the rule or you know what you are doing. As this can lead to items being unfiltered and caught in the 'Catch All' error rule showing PINK.

The filter has many rules that are in a very specific order to implement priorities, as one item can always be only handled by one rule. You can always right-click rules to view their priority and compare it to other rules. Normal existing rules can not have their priority changed, but new additional custom rules that you can create can have their priority edited!

Importing someone else's filter: if follow a filter on PoE, you can go to their Profile page and check if they have their filter saved publicly on FilterBlade (include the '#1234' discriminator at the end of the username for most accounts, leave '#1234' off for older legacy accounts!). If it's private you may try asking them. Otherwise, you're out of luck.

Head to the FilterBlade Discord and post a message in the applicable PoE1/PoE2 filter questions channel with name of the filter, approximate last known good state that needs recovery, and your copied UUID. (Can wait for a reponse to send the UUID and delete after they've got it). One of the mods will attempt to recover the filter and provide a .save file.

You can only upload into filterblade via a 'SaveFile' as this contains all the information on the changes made to the stock filter that got you to the current state. Think of the save file as a list of instructions on what to do for it to go from A - B. If you have the savefile you can go to Advanced > Test Local Filter > Load filter from saveFile.

We store filters by your account-name. If your name changed, you basically count as a different person. Your best option is to make all of your filters public on FilterBlade before changing your name and then loading them from the Profile page on FilterBlade into your new account. We value user privacy and will never migrate any private saves.

covered: Many Players also choose to use rares for the 'Chaos Recipe'. This is a safe and consistent way to make currency, especially early on in the league. For that you need to sell a full equipment of rares (boots, gloves, helm, 2 rings, 1 amulet, belt, armor, weapon+shield or a 2h weapon) of itemlevel 60+ (found in act 9 or later). The vendor will reward you with a Chaos Orb. If all items are unidentified, he'll give you 2 Chaos Orbs.

Rare items can be crazy strong. That being said it's very tedious to pick, identify and treat (sell/price/keep) rare items. It takes a lot of practice and knowledge to quickly price rare items and there's a lot of factors, such as league type, age, meta, itemlevel, that affects it.

'Rare accessories' are a fairly common drop, but they are tiny and most builds cover their stats and resists through rare accessories. This makes these rares a much more lucrative pick-ups than non-accessoires rares. On top of that they are usually the bottleneck for chaos recipes.

All top tier items have the same white background and drop-sound. They also come with a red beam and a huge red star on the minimap. These items include top tier currencies, valuable uniques, great divination cards, reliquary keys and everything else that is worth a LOT.

It should be noted that other items without the white background can be just as, if not more valuable. However, with other items it often comes down to mods, luck and crafting, while the white background items are pretty much always great!

There are hundreds of uniques! Some are in high demand, others are worthless or very niche. The filter can't distinguish between uniques with the same baseType. Bases with a blue or purple beam/map icon could potentially be very expensive.

Their powerful effects aside high currencies act as trade goods for players. Chaos Orbs and Divine Orbs are pretty much the standard way to pay for most trades. These are desired drops and it's almost always recommended to pick them up.

Divination cards grant you a specific item reward upon completing the set. Each card type drops in specific zones or by specific enemies, allowing players to farm them (although some cards can be super rare regardless).

The site is updated every 4 hours and the tiering of the items may differ. Items might change their tier based on high or low demand. Note that you have to redownload/sync the filter to get the latest economy data!

The blue or purple map icons and beams signalize that are drop CAN be quite valuable... if you're lucky. A unique Leather Belt can very very rarely be an expensive headhunter and the filter can't tell them apart.

Note that you can corrupt a skillgem for a chance to receive extra gemlevels. This way you can create level 21 gems. You can also sell a level 20 gem and a gemcutter Prisms to receive a level 1 20% quality gem.

Items have a sound that is linked to their value-tier. All high tier currencies make the same sound. When you hear it - you know 'something dropped'. You can click on the currency preview to hear the sound
Map fragment open a unique encounter if used if the other pieces of the set. Most scarabs on the other hand add both challenge and reward to a map encounter. Some of these can be very pricy!
Generally speaking the purple icon is used for the items with a higher chance to be good. On top of that the small blue stars are usually indicative of a basetypes with good boss-drops.
You can change all of these settings in the customizer screen here. To quickly jump to the settings for a certain item, right click the item label or CTRL+click the item.
Most fragments can also be added onto a map to increase it's quantity, if you're not interested in the encounter itself. This is commonly done with sacrifice fragments.
Maps gain more highlight as they gain tiers. High tier (11+) and top tier (16) maps have different sounds. The filter highlights map tier upgrades with an extra color.
Currently expensive gems are highlighted by the filter. Additionally the filter will highlight gems with special properties, such as higher levels, quality etc.
Useful currency that drops while leveling. These rules have priority over normal currency rules, but only apply in areas under level 68. Great for new leagues!
The Text color is orange, instead of yellow, if the itemLevel is 75 or above, meaning that you can use the item for the Regal recipe instead of the chaos one.
The divination card economy is quite volatile. Periodically returning to FilterBlade and redownloading the latest filter is recommended to stay up-to-date.
Consume uniques in the Timeless Conflict (Legion) with Enshrouding Crystals. A random 'vestigial' unique will hatch - empowered by the consumed unique.
These rares are popular in the current meta and are often small pickups. Getting the right stats on these makes them quite valuable.
Don't underrate chance orbs! You can buy maps from Kirac at the start of the league to quickly progress through the atlas!
The filter highlights map drops of a higher tier than the one you're in with extra highlight (disabled on some styles)
The economy sometimes has large meta-shifts! A cheap unique can become very expensive very fast (or vice versa)!
Note: random non-quality skillgems are hidden on higher strictnesses, since they can be purachased from an NPC.
They also come with a minimap-icon. The icons can be seen next to the item preview labels on FilterBlade.
Filterblade tiering is based on the ingame economy. It's a good practice to update the filter weekly.
Divination Cards have vastly different price and rarity ranges and are tiered based on their value.
Alterations, jeweller's and chromatics can also be reliably obtained by doing vendor recipes.
You can find gold all throughout the game. It's picked up automatically as you walk over it.
Rather common, but unless sold in bulk, not too expensive. Often used in basic crafting.
Dead Man's Sulphur, Ducats and all kind of precious items can be found on the seafloor!
Quality on gems influences each gem in a different way. Consult the wiki for details.
Quality gems can be sold in bulk to NPCs to get gemcutter prisms

This section is designed to be foolproof. It will have no effect on 6-links, endgame items, elder/shaper items, uniques etc), abyss belts, fishing rods and other special bases. These sections frequently feature the 'strictness' dropdown menu. This tool defines how many rules are overwritten by your custom rules. I recommend playing around with the loot simulator, while switching back and forth to the customizer to get familiar with this section

It's recommended to at least use the threshold of 14. This allows you to get 1 glassblower per 3 mid quality flasks. Note that glassblowers can also be acquired by buying it for 8 whetstones from vendors and drop naturally, so the recipe is not very efficient. That being said, glassblowers are in high demand at the start of the league, not only for quality, but also to apply instilling orb recipes onto the player flasks.

The filter will check identified rares for interesting mod combinations and highlight these items. By setting this rule to HIDE all items that have NOT passed the 'interesting identified mods check' will be hidden. This is useful if you're still searching for specific rare combinations, but would like to reduce the number of items visible.

By selling a total of 40% quality worth of gems with a specific tag (such as fire) together with a Wand, Sceptre, Rune Dagger or Staff you will be rewarded with a weapon with a +1 GLOBAL level to ALL tagged spell gems. This is a powerful caster weapon early in the endgame.

It's more efficient to pick up small RGB-items. This recipe is mostly useful during the early stages of a league/character progression. Later on the player usually finds enough natural chromatic orbs to sustain their coloring needs, without needing to do recipes.

By adding e.g. 'GG', all 4-links will need to at least have 2 green colors to get highlighted. You can add one or multiple combinations of 'R', 'G' and 'B'. This is very useful to hide uninteresting linked items.

The filter comes with a system to check if an identified rare has interesting stat combos. Identified rares drop rarely, but if NO statcombo was detected, you might consider hiding them. This can be done here.
1 Chromatic orb - reward for selling an item with a Red-Green-Blue socket group. The 3 colors need to be linked in order and other sockets don't matter. Hover over the scroll left for more info.
High level, specific crafting bases are in high demand early in the league and can be useful in SSF environments. This section handles non-influenced versions of these items.
Disabling recipe item rules will NOT hide uniques, 6links, interesting synthesised items etc. Priorities are handled internally and you don't need to worry about them.
By default the filter will hide all (unidentified) corrupted/mirrored rares without an implicit. This of course excludes 6-links and all kinds of other exotic items
Designed to highlight lower tiers (Tier C and lower) divination cards if they drop in a stack. Useful, if you want to see the cards only if they're stacked.
Note: The section 'hide and highlight rares by type' section can be used to achieve the same result, while also having control over classes and levels.
Some item classes like 'Jewels' are completely covered through the class-based filtering below and don't need representing through the matrix.
1 Gemcutter's Prism - reward for selling a single gem with 20% quality gem or multiple gems with a combined total of 40% quality to a vendor.
Quickly highlight bases by adding a custom rule! If you need more power and options, there's a lot more custom rules lower in the customizer
This section combines 30 different rules that will highlight the best available life, mana and hybrid flasks, during your Campaign progress.
Decorators highlight specific characteristics of an item, by changing the appearance, without deciding whether it is hidden or shown.
Augment the filter with entirely new rules, such as 'only show AR and AR/EV armors', 'highlight all rare axes' and 'hide all wands'
Itemlevel matters a LOT. Crafting bases are grouped by level. Example: Any Gloves will be part of and ONLY of the level 85 rules.
1 Glassblower's Bauble - reward for selling a single 20% quality flask or multiple quality flasks with a total quality of 40%.
These rules are enabled in higher strictness. They hide lower rares if they drop in high level zones.
By default rares have a higher evaluation priority than chromatic recipes. This can be changed here.
Hide uninteresting items, such as bows for melee characters or melee weapons for casters.
Hide all remaining identified items that were not highlighted by the mod filtering rules.
Card added here will receive a higher highlight if dropped in a stack!
